newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says it easing West Bank, Gaza closure.
newsitem.headline: Israel says it easing West Bank, Gaza closure.

text.p: Israel said on Thursday it was easing its closure of the West Bank and Gaza Strip and allowing about 35,000 Palestinians to work in the Jewish state.

"Beginning this Sunday, about 35,000 workers from Judea, Samaria (the West Bank) and Gaza will be permitted to work in Israel and all internal closures in Judea and Samaria will be lifted, except for the city of Nablus," said a spokesman for Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.
Asked about the announcement, Major General Abdelrazeq al-Majayda, commander of Palestinian police forces in Gaza, told Reuters: "We were not informed about this. We have no idea."
About 19,500 Palestinians worked in Israel before last month's eruption of violence that killed 60 Arabs and 15 Jews.
It was unclear how long it would take Israel to carry out security checks and issue work permits to 35,000 labourers.

Israel, which banned most Palestinians from its territory after Moslem suicide bombings in February and March, imposed restrictions on Arabs travelling between West Bank cities, after the September clashes.
Those "internal closures" have already been lifted from most of the cities.
In a statement, the spokesman said Mordechai decided to ease restrictions "in order to reduce the hardship of the Palestinian population...and the Palestinian economy".

But Morechai instructed the Israeli army in the West Bank and Gaza to "remain in their reinforced deployment, so that they can provide a suitable response to any possible development," the spokesman said.
In addition to the entry of the workers, Israel will open two Gaza crossings, Karni and Sufa, for the passage of goods to and from Gaza, he said.

"The defence minister expressed his hope that the opening of the closures and the easing of the current restrictions, will contribute to a positive atmosphere between Israel and the Palestinian Authority," the statement said.
Israel and the Palestinians are currently negotiating how to carry out a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank city of Hebron.
